Last Friday (21st), a Hong Kong Alliance case was handed down its verdict. In the early morning, police took away a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing in a police vehicle. In response to enquiries, the police said the woman had been arrested on three charges: "behaviour in a public place disturbing public order", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty", and "with seditious intent".

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than fifty people had already been queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the wait, a plainclothes officer pointed out a woman in the queue as "suspected of wearing clothing with seditious intent", and promptly took her onto a police vehicle. As officers escorted the woman away, multiple officers repeatedly told reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled the orange cordon tape towards the direction of Ying Wa Lane. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, the cordon tape was immediately retracted. A "court observation volunteer" who had been queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt printed with Japanese characters at the time.

Citizen News (集誌社) made enquiries to the police regarding the reason the woman was taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman had been arrested on suspicion of "behaviour in a public place disturbing public order", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty", and "with seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
